sections.title: aki's counterpart for things
sections.content: You already know aki ("who") for attaching a clause to a person. ami is the same idea for things and ideas: "which, that". Everything after ami conjugates completely normally, exactly like after aki. When ami is the OBJECT of its own clause, it takes the accusative -t, just like any other object: ami -> amit.

items.spanish: Ez az a könyv, amit olvasok.
items.english: This is the book that I'm reading.

items.spanish: A regény, ami az asztalon van, nagyon izgalmas.
items.english: The novel that's on the table is very exciting.

sections.content: Use ami/amit for things, ideas, and anything that isn't a person; use aki for people. Before you speak, quickly ask yourself "person or thing?" — this is one of the most common mix-ups for learners.
